correctness.rationale: For any finite Zimin word, the ruler identity z_j=1+nu_2(j) proves palindromicity and uniqueness of each linear factor's maximum symbol, excluding every linear Abelian square. A circular Abelian square must cross the original join. After reversal, an off-center crossing would give P(y+2x)-P(y)=2P(x) for x,y>=1. The factor on the left has length 2x and necessarily contains an index divisible by 2^(floor(log_2(x))+1), and therefore a symbol greater than all symbols in the prefix x represented on the right. This contradiction rules out every off-center start. The unique centered occurrence exists at every 1<=d<=floor(N/2). Its nonwrapping cuts are exactly d<=c<=N-d, yielding min(c,N-c), and a three-block Abelian cube would create two different starts at the same d. Exhaustive independent Counter/prefix methods through n=8 check all (i,d), all 502 linear cuts, and all admissible cyclic cubes. The theorem remains an all-order mathematical proof; finite scans are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: The exact indexed circular Abelian-square spectrum, tent-shaped rotation profile, and cyclic Abelian-cube exclusion do not follow from the linear maximal Abelian-squarefree property documented by Cummings--Mays and Bullock, or from the crucial-word Abelian-power constructions of Glen--Halldorsson--Kitaev. A separate prior historical result for ordinary circular tandem squares does not cover Abelian squares: ordinary equality implies equal Parikh vectors, but not conversely. A checked 21-letter Abelian-squarefree palindrome shows that even palindrome+linear avoidance need not force unique centered cyclic anagram squares. Actual targeted web searches and published-finding corpus semantic searches found no matching theorem. The conclusion is best-knowledge originality, not exhaustive proof of historical priority.

value.rationale: This exact all-order theorem resolves the natural cyclic repetition profile of the classical recursively palindromic and linearly Abelian-squarefree Zimin family, determining every allowed half-length and its unique center, the full linear-cut distribution, and total absence of circular Abelian cubes. The proof isolates the 2-adic prefix-versus-window obstruction that drives the rigidity. The result is not merely restating linear avoidance: other linearly Abelian-squarefree palindromes have extra off-center cyclic Abelian squares, as witnessed explicitly. It supplies a reusable structural boundary between linear repetition avoidance and circular anagram repetitions rather than a gratuitous finite table.
